_meta.population: W-H PR-3b: the residual openness assertions the lot-1 spec (prose_lampiran2_wh_pr3b_2026_09_15, which cured editorial.headline/standfirst/body/pullQuote and whatYouNeed) did not cover, found by a manual sweep of every string field of intel_2026 for the 8 specialised-retail codes with the same regex used on PR-3a: `PMA status: (Open|Terbuka)|open to (foreign|PMA)|100 ?% (foreign|PMA|open)|fully open|PMA[- ]friendly|your PT PMA|Typical structure: PT PMA|PT PMA setup|foreign[- ]owned (shop|store|retail)`, case-insensitive. Five codes' zantaraOpener still opened with a national-openness claim (four with the template 'Nationally this carries PMA status: Open', one — 47242 — with '100% open to PMA'). 47242's baliContext separately framed the code as 'the typical PMA use case' and described a foreign-owned bakery business, which the allocation makes impossible.
_meta.no_new_claims: Every replacement states only the record's own allocation (Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran II entry 46) and that a PT PMA cannot register the code — the same fact already carried on the record's own pma_official_basis and pma_kondisi. No price, date or percentage other than 0 is added. 47242's baliContext drops the now-false PMA business-tip content (BPOM cold-chain advice framed for a foreign-owned bakery, pairing with a manufacturing code) and keeps only the allocation fact plus the generalist-retail distinction already adjudicated in this lane's allocation spec (`excluded.generalist_retail_never_touched`).

zantaraOpener.new: Opening a bakery shop in Bali? KBLI 47242 — retail of bread, dry cakes and wet cakes as a specialised store — is allocated to Koperasi and UMKM under Perpres 49/2021's Lampiran II, so a PT PMA cannot register it. Here's what that means for your business.

baliContext.old_excerpt: Premium bakery chains targeting the expat and tourist market are the typical
baliContext.new: This activity — retail of bread, dry cakes and wet cakes as a specialised store — is allocated to Koperasi and UMKM under Perpres 49/2021's Lampiran II entry 46. The reservation is nationwide, not a Bali-specific restriction: a PT PMA cannot register this code anywhere in Indonesia, including Bali. Selling the same goods inside a supermarket or general store uses a different KBLI, outside this allocation.
